data.title: Biocon gets Brazilian regulator nod for biosimilar Pertuzumab for breast cancer treatment
data.description:
Biocon Ltd on Friday said Hertuzo, a biosimilar Pertuzumab licensed to its partner Bionovis, has received approval from Brazilian regulator ANVISA for treating HER2-positive breast cancer.

The approval builds on Biocon's 10-year productive development partnership (PDP) in Brazil through a consortium with Bionovis and public pharmaceutical laboratory Bahiafarma, the company said in a statement.

Through the PDP, the consortium has an opportunity to supply locally manufactured biosimilar Pertuzumab to Brazil's public healthcare market, potentially broadening access and delivering savings to the healthcare system, the Bengaluru-based company said.

The nod follows recent approvals for Biocon's biosimilar Pertuzumab from the US Food and Drug Administration and the European Commission.

Susheel Umesh, Chief Commercial Officer for Emerging Markets and Head of Global API & Global BD at Biocon, said the ANVISA approval underscores the company's scientific and regulatory capabilities and the growing strength of its global oncology portfolio.

It enables the company to advance its PDP partnership with Bionovis and Bahiafarma, expanding access at scale to an affordable, high-quality biologic therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer patients in Brazil, he added.

data.title: Sensex falls 764 points, Nifty slips below 25,700 as IT, financials drag
data.description:
Benchmark indices traded sharply lower in afternoon trade on Friday as information technology and financial stocks declined, while the broader market held up better.

At 1.16 pm, the Sensex was at 83,564.55, down 764.04 points or 0.91 per cent from its previous close of 84,328.59. The index had opened at 84,093.24. The Nifty was at 25,673.60, down 210.90 points or 0.81 per cent from its previous close of 25,884.50. It had opened at 25,839.25.

Among Nifty 50 gainers, Bharat Electronics rose 1.85 per cent to ₹412. Titan gained 1.47 per cent to ₹4,699, JSW Steel added 0.94 per cent to ₹1,315.20, Trent rose 0.75 per cent to ₹3,287 and Hindustan Unilever gained 0.56 per cent to ₹2,142.70.

Shriram Finance led the losers, falling 3.73 per cent to ₹926. Bajaj Auto declined 2.80 per cent to ₹10,546, HCLTech fell 2.19 per cent to ₹1,436.40, Infosys lost 2.13 per cent to ₹1,157.80 and Bharti Airtel slipped 1.88 per cent to ₹2,063.

Among sectoral indices, Nifty IT was the worst performer, according to SBI Securities, as investors booked profits after Thursday’s sharp rally. Nifty India Defence was the best performer. On the BSE, 2,414 stocks advanced and 1,781 declined, while 257 were unchanged. The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 0.60 per cent and the Smallcap 100 gained 0.95 per cent. Within the Nifty, 15 stocks advanced and 35 declined.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said the market’s mood reflected pressure on several fronts. “The cautious tone reflects a combination of rising crude prices, a weaker rupee and lingering uncertainty over the India-US trade negotiations,” he said. He added that export-oriented sectors, particularly IT, remain vulnerable to the outlook for bilateral trade.

The rupee was trading around 92.56 to the dollar, weaker by about 0.1 per cent. Brent crude settled 2.07 per cent higher at $96.57 a barrel on Thursday, its highest since November 6, after reports of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and an attack on a Saudi refinery. Brent is still nearly 20 per cent lower for November. WTI crude was near $85.75. For India, a major energy importer, higher oil prices can raise the import bill and add to inflation concerns. OPEC+ is expected to keep production targets unchanged through March 2027 ahead of its meeting on Sunday.

On the BSE, 86 stocks hit 52-week highs and 107 hit lows. In all, 147 stocks were locked in the upper circuit and 176 in the lower circuit.

On the charts, SBI Securities placed Nifty support at 25,550-25,570 and resistance at 25,860-25,880. A fall below 25,550 could take the index to 25,380-25,400, it said. For the Sensex, it placed support at 83,300 and resistance at 84,200. In the options market, SBI Securities noted “meaningful call writing witnessed across 25800 & 25900 strikes,” while the 25,700 put strike has substantial open interest.

Commodities moved higher. MCX gold futures were near ₹1,24,140 per 10 grams, up about 1.5 per cent, and MCX silver was near ₹1,51,380 per kg, up about 3.8 per cent. MCX crude oil was near ₹7,960, up about 1.1 per cent. Gold was recovering from a 15-month low hit earlier this week. Enrich Money said a softer US dollar and a rebound in technology stocks supported prices, though expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate increases remain a headwind.

Bank Nifty opened near 63,326 and was holding above the 63,000-63,200 support zone, according to Enrich Money.

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus.com, advised investors in precious metals to “avoid chasing sharp daily rallies” and to consider staggered accumulation and sensible position sizing.

data.title: French Inflation Slides on Drop in Fuel Prices — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl

Inflation in France fell more than expected in November as fuel prices declined, but remained too high for the European Central Bank, which next month is expected to raise its key interest rate for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

Inflation in France climbed to its highest level in nearly three years in October, from an annual rate of just 1.1% in February, before the first U.S. airstrikes on Iran.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation, for instance, fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

It comes as France's economy appears to have been hit harder by the war than its neighbors. Gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, dented by a drop in exports and lower private investment.

Investors have grown more concerned in recent months over the country's public finances, which sent government bond yields rising. Those higher bond yields, while ratcheting up nervousness around the economy, could help the ECB as they tighten monetary conditions before the central bank needs to raise rates.

French consumer spending was flat on month in October, data also published Friday showed, coming in the month when consumer confidence hit its lowest level in more than three years. While surveys of purchasing managers showed steady economic growth in Germany, there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

In neighboring Spain, inflation also declined notably in November, falling to 4.1% from 4.9% in October, data published Friday showed.

data.title: Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools
data.description:
(08:33 GMT) *Meituan 3Q Rev CNY115.55B Vs. CNY95.06B >3690.HK
(08:34 GMT) *Meituan 3Q Net CNY2.07B Vs. Loss CNY18.63B >3690.HK
(08:49 GMT) Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools

By Tracy Qu

Meituan's profit was largely stable sequentially amid higher revenue in the third quarter as China's top food-delivery company continued to recover from a brutal price war.

The Beijing-based company on Friday said net profit was 2.07 billion yuan, equivalent to $310.7 million, for the three months ended September. It recorded a 2.15 billion yuan net profit in the second quarter and net loss of 18.63 billion yuan a year ago.

Revenue climbed 22% from a year earlier to 115.55 billion yuan.

The results beat market expectations. Analysts had expected net profit of 354.7 million yuan on revenue of 113.56 billion yuan, according to a FactSet-compiled consensus.

Meituan has been locked in a food-delivery price war since last year as Alibaba Group and JD.com pushed to gain more market share. Competition has normalized in recent quarters.

data.title: Euro zone bond yields rise with oil after choppy week for shares
data.description:
Euro zone yields rose on Friday, as investors returned to equity markets and oil prices were set to snap a three-week losing streak.

After a choppy week for shares, which sent many market participants in search of safe-haven assets, Germany's 10-year bond yield (DE10YT=RR), the benchmark for the euro zone, rose 1.8 basis points (bps) to 3.284%.

As a more risk-on environment returned, yields were also supported by Thursday's publication of minutes from the European Central Bank's October meeting, which showed that some policymakers were leaning towards an interest rate hike but opted for a delay to collect more evidence on inflation risks.

Money markets price in two ECB rate increases of 25 bps by June 2027, LSEG data showed.

Brent crude oil futures were up 1.2% as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supply from the conflict-hit Middle East.

The 2-year German Schatz yield was steady at 3.076%. (DE2YT=RR)

Other euro zone yields were mixed. France's 10-year yield seesawed and was last down 1.6 bps at 4.727% while Italy's was little changed at 4.339%. , (FR10YT=RR)

Euro zone yields were still set for a weekly drop.

data.title: Lumibird Shares Surge After Thales Targets Majority Stake in $483 Million Laser Deal
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

Shares in laser-technology company Lumibird soared after Thales said it was in exclusive talks to buy a majority stake that would value its photonics division at around 440 million euros, including debt, equivalent to $482.6 million.

In opening European trade, shares were 18.5% higher at 29.1 euros, lifting their year-to-date gains to 37%.

Aerospace-and-defense group Thales said Friday that it planned to buy a 51.6% stake in Lumibird from its chief executive officer and majority shareholder, Marc Le Flohic. Thales said the deal valued Lumibird at 30.10 euros a share. Lumibird shares closed Thursday at 24.55 euros. Thales expects to close the deal in the second quarter of next year.

The price per share paid could rise to 32.66 euros, depending on the completion of the sale of Lumibird's medical division.

Thales said the deal would create a European photonics platform and help it develop laser-directed energy weapons.

The company will later file a tender offer for all Lumibird shares that it doesn't hold and expects to complete this in the second half of 2027, it said.

data.title: Rheinmetall Gets $810 Million Tank Order From Romania
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Rheinmetall said it received an order valued at 738 million euros ($809.5 million) to supply dozens of its Lynx tanks to Romania, a key growth market for the German defense contractor.

The company said Friday that Romania placed an additional order for 66 Lynx combat vehicles under a framework contract signed in May. The Romanian fleet will mainly consist of infantry-fighting vehicles, supplemented by armored mortar, command post and medical variant vehicles, Rheinmetall added.

Romania had already ordered an initial batch of 232 vehicles when the broader framework contract--covering 298 Lynx vehicles in total--was first awarded.

The company said it is investing several hundred million euros in Romania to fulfill the orders it received there.

Rheinmetall has benefited in recent years from a flurry of contracts as European governments stepped up defense spending, but procurement delays for some of them prompted the company to cut its annual guidance twice this year.

data.title: Finland Q3 GDP Expands Less Than Estimated
data.description:
HELSINKI (dpa-AFX) - Finland's economy grew less than initially estimated in the third quarter, the latest data from Statistics Finland showed on Friday.

Gross domestic product advanced a seasonally and working-day-adjusted 0.3 percent sequentially in the third quarter, after rising 0.2 percent in the previous quarter. In the flash estimate, the expansion was 0.5 percent.

The expenditure breakdown showed that private consumption decreased by 0.2 percent compared to the second quarter, while government consumption was 0.3 percent higher. Gross fixed capital formation grew 7.5 percent, with public investments rising by 33.1 percent. Net foreign demand was not favorable as exports fell 5.5 percent amid a 5.1 percent increase in imports.

On an annual basis, economic growth improved to 1.5 percent from 1.2 percent in the previous quarter.

data.title: Uber Secures Approximately 87% of Delivery Hero Shares Following End of Additional Acceptance Period
data.description:
Uber International Technologies II Corporation (the “Bidder”), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Uber Technologies, Inc. (; together with its subsidiaries, including the Bidder, “Uber”), today announced the final results of its voluntary public takeover offer for all outstanding registered shares of Delivery Hero SE (“Delivery Hero”, ISIN DE000A2E4K43) not already held by the Bidder (the “Offer”).

By the end of the additional acceptance period, which expired on November 24, 2026, at 24:00 hours (Frankfurt am Main local time) / 18:00 hours (New York local time), Uber secured a total of approximately 87.13% of Delivery Hero’s share capital.

“We’re excited to see such strong support from Delivery Hero shareholders, reinforcing the confidence already expressed by the company’s Management Board and Supervisory Board,” said Dara Khosrowshahi, CEO of Uber. “Bringing our companies closer together creates more value for consumers, merchants and earners alike, and we’re excited to get to work.”

The transaction is subject to the remaining offer conditions, namely the receipt of required merger control and other regulatory clearances, as set out in full in the Offer Document. Closing is expected in the second half of 2027.

About Uber

Uber’s mission is to create opportunity through movement. We started in 2010 to solve a simple problem: how do you get access to a ride at the touch of a button? More than 83 billion trips later, we’re building products to get people closer to where they want to be. By changing how people, food, and things move through cities, Uber is a platform that opens up the world to new possibilities.

data.title: Taiwan Raises 2026 Growth Forecasts as AI Exports Surge
data.description:
(08:06 GMT) *Taiwan Revises 3Q GDP To +14.39% On Year Vs +14.36% Estimate
(08:06 GMT) *Taiwan Revises 3Q GDP To +2.86% On Quarter Vs +3.21% Estimate
(08:07 GMT) *Taiwan 2026 GDP Forecast +13.28%
(08:07 GMT) *Taiwan 2027 Real GDP Forecast +6.51%
(08:45 GMT) Taiwan Raises 2026 Growth Forecasts as AI Exports Surge

By Sherry Qin

Taiwan revised its annual growth forecast higher as the wider use of artificial intelligence fueled demand for its technology exports.

The economy is projected to grow 13.28% this year, up from a previous forecast of 11.05%, the statistics bureau said Friday. The bureau also raised its estimate of third-quarter growth to 14.39% from a year earlier, from a preliminary reading of 14.36%.

Global cloud providers are expanding their AI infrastructure as more businesses adopt systems that can carry out tasks in multiple steps, the bureau said. Taiwan's exports of advanced technology hardware have surged as shortages have pushed up prices for components such as memory chips and substrates.

The bureau expects growth to slow to 6.51% in 2027.

A slowdown in U.S. spending on AI, particularly on data-center construction, could weaken demand for advanced chips made in Taiwan. Tighter U.S. controls on advanced chip exports could also disrupt supply chains and curb demand in Southeast Asia, which accounts for 19% of Taiwan's exports, HSBC analysts said in a recent note.

"Although expanded U.S. AI export controls and potential tighter regulation by local governments in response to residents' opposition to data center construction could affect the implementation costs and timelines of related investments, the trajectory of AI development remains firmly established," it said.

Taiwan also faces the prospect of new U.S. tariffs. The Trump administration on Wednesday proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including Taiwan, over industrial policies it says hurt U.S. businesses. Taiwan said Thursday it was confident it could retain its existing 15% U.S. tariff rate and would work to preserve the terms of earlier agreements.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: AcouSort selected to present at HealthTech Investor Summit
data.description:
AcouSort has been invited to participate in the pitch program at the HealthTech Investor Summit in Bruges on December 1-2, where CEO Torsten Freltoft will present the company and its acoustofluidic technology to an audience of investors and industry representatives.

The HealthTech Investor Summit brings together companies, investors and stakeholders within the healthtech and life science sectors. AcouSort’s participation provides an opportunity to present the company’s technology platform and commercial strategy, with a particular focus on the potential of acoustofluidics to enable automated and integrated sample preparation in future diagnostic and life science applications.

“We are very pleased to have been invited to present AcouSort at the HealthTech Investor Summit. It is an excellent opportunity for presenting our technology and commercial strategy to an investor audience and to highlight the role we believe acoustofluidics can play in the continued automation of sample preparation in life science and diagnostics,” says Torsten Freltoft, CEO of AcouSort.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ABOUT ACOUSORT, PLEASE CONTACT:

Torsten Freltoft, CEO

Telephone: +45 2045 0854

E-mail: torsten.freltoft@acousort.com

ABOUT ACOUSORT

AcouSort AB (corporate registration number 556824-1037) is an innovative technology company focusing on developing products and solutions for integrated preparation of biological samples. With the help of sound waves, the company's products can separate blood cells, concentrate, purify, and stain cells, exosomes, and bacteria from biological samples. The technology of the company's products is acoustofluidics, where sound waves and microfluidics enable automated handling of samples in a range of application areas, from research on new biomarkers to the development of new diagnostic systems for near-patient testing – so-called Point-of Care (POC) systems. The company's commercialization strategy is based on the already proven business model of providing separation modules to diagnostic system manufacturers for integrated sample preparation as well as to continue the commercialization of the company's research instruments. With the help of the company's products and development of point-of-care tests, new diagnostic systems and treatments are enabled, addressing some of the most challenging disease areas of our time: cancer, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular diseases. AcouSort is listed at Nasdaq First North Growth Market. The company’s Certified Adviser is Tapper Partners AB.

data.title: Antipodean Currencies Rise Amid Risk-On Mood
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - The antipodean currencies such as the Australia and the New Zealand dollars strengthened against their major currencies in the Asian session on Friday, as Asian stock markets traded higher as traders return to buy semiconductor and technology stocks on stabilized sentiment over AI trade following a sharp sell-off earlier in the week. They also stepped in to pick up recently beaten-down shares.

Meanwhile, caution prevails as the U.S. proposes tariffs on major trading partners and on reports that Nvidia has ordered manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries amid U.S. efforts to restrict AI chip flows to China.

Escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East continues to weigh on market sentiment after Yemen's Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery Ras Raura and the petromonarchy's financial district in the capital Riyadh. Iran also reported that several vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz had struck mines.

As concerns about more international trade in artificial intelligence (AI) diminish, copper futures are up about 7% to close at $5.75.

Due to a notable rebound in copper prices, the Australian dollar performs better overall, strengthening the cross.

Crude oil prices rose amid supply concerns after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have hit Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and two ships hit mines laid by the Iranian's in the Strait of Hormuz. The US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained $0.35 or 0.4 percent to $84.03 a barrel.

In the Asian trading today, the Australian dollar rose to 1-week highs of 0.6678 against the U.S. dollar and 106.36 against the yen, from yesterday's closing quotes of 0.6635 and 105.37, respectively. If the aussie extends its uptrend, it is likely to find resistance around 0.69 against the greenback and 110.00 against the yen.

Against the euro, the Canada and the New Zealand dollars, the aussie advanced to 2-day highs of 1.6448, 0.9502 and 1.2159 from Thursday's closing quotes of 1.6534, 0.9453 and 1.2067, respectively. The aussie may test resistance around 1.63 against the euro, 0.97 against the loonie and 1.23 against the kiwi.

The NZ dollar rose to 1-week highs of 0.5505 against 87.64 against the yen, from 2-day lows of 0.5456 and 86.94, respectively. If the kiwi extends its uptrend, it is likely to find resistance around 0.56 against the greenback and 88.00 against the yen.

Against the euro, the kiwi advanced to a 4-day high of 1.9940 from an early 4-day low of 2.0090. The kiwi may test resistance around the 1.79 region.

Looking ahead, German jobs data for November, the European Central Bank consumer inflation expectations for October and Eurozone economic sentiment for November are slated for release in the European session.

In the New York session, Canada current account for the third quarter, U.S. goods trade balance for October, U.S. retail and wholesale inventories for October, are set to be released.

data.title: Precious Metals Jump on Easing AI Jitters — Market Talk
data.description: Precious metal prices jump as investors return to the AI trade and global stocks rebound, boosting risk appetite across markets. Gold futures rise 3.8% to $3,671.90 a troy ounce, while silver soars 10.1% to $44.11 an ounce. Platinum is up 8.5% to $1,348.50 an ounce. "Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank say. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure." Still, the broader macroeconomic picture remains challenging, with traders expecting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December and potentially next year as well. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

data.title: Indonesian nickel boss possibly involved in treason against Prabowo's government, official says
data.description:
Indonesian nickel businessman Arif Kurniawan was possibly involved in treason against President Prabowo Subianto's government, the head of the government's communications office was quoted by state news agency Antara as saying on Friday.

The comment about former Glencore trader Arif, named this week as a criminal suspect in alleged money laundering from 2021 to 2026 stemming from corrupt practices when obtaining a mining permit, follows an ongoing investigation launched after a former police chief was accused of wiretapping Prabowo.

Communications head Syahganda Nainggolan said Arif served as an "intellectual actor" in the operation, indicating that he was involved in orchestrating it. He added that Arif might already have fled to China, Antara reported.

"We see indications that a mining magnate, whose name is Arif Kurniawan, is among the intellectual actors because those intellectual actors are invariably backed by politics and oligarchic interests," he said.

Syahganda did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday. Reuters was unable to identify Arif's legal representatives and attempts to reach him by phone were unsuccessful.

According to the prosecutors, a mining businessman with the initials AK, identified by local media as Arif, controlled at least six nickel mining companies in Southeast Sulawesi, with licenses covering more than 4,000 hectares of mining concessions.

Local media have referred to Arif as a "nickel king".

The ongoing treason investigation was triggered by the arrest and dismissal of Indonesia's former police chief, Listyo Sigit Prabowo. He was charged with treason this week.

Listyo, who is not related to the president, allegedly ordered the unauthorised wiretapping of several figures, including Prabowo, police said.

The ousted police chief was widely regarded as being close to Prabowo's predecessor Joko Widodo, and the treason allegations have fueled speculation that ties between Prabowo and Widodo have become strained.

Treason charges are rare in Indonesia and carry a maximum penalty of death, Indonesian law stipulates.
